topics.title: Probability
topics.summary: Chance from countable outcomes to distributions; each exploration uses small games and explicit assumptions.

topics.title: Statistics and inference
topics.summary: Describe data, sample honestly and interpret uncertainty without turning thresholds into truths.

topics.title: Stochastic processes
topics.summary: Random paths, memory, arrivals and queues in small toy worlds.

topics.title: Information theory
topics.summary: Bits, surprise, compression and noisy clues as mathematical measures of uncertainty.

topics.title: Game theory and social choice
topics.summary: Strategic choices and collective rankings explored through small transparent games and ballots.

topics.title: Mathematical modelling
topics.summary: Build, test and critique models through art, sound, networks and physical sketches.

articles.title: A deck, a die, and the sample space
articles.hook: A homemade board game has two dice but only one reroll.
articles.outcome: List outcomes and distinguish event from outcome.
articles.formula: P(A)=|A|/|Omega| for equally likely elementary outcomes
articles.visual: Grid of ordered die pairs with highlighted event.
articles.proof: Derive finite equiprobable rule; unequal likelihood is deferred.

articles.title: Why two chances can overlap
articles.hook: Count how often a card is red or a face card.
articles.outcome: Use inclusion-exclusion without double counting.
articles.visual: Venn diagram and enumerated card table.
articles.proof: Derive by partitioning disjoint regions.

articles.title: The clue changes the denominator
articles.hook: A mystery card is known to be a heart.
articles.outcome: Rebuild a sample space after conditioning.
articles.visual: Card grid that fades excluded outcomes.
articles.proof: Derive finite conditioning and state positive-denominator condition.

articles.title: Bayes with two bags of marbles
articles.hook: One of two bags was chosen before a blue marble appeared.
articles.outcome: Update prior odds using the likelihood ratio.
articles.formula: posterior odds=prior odds x likelihood ratio
articles.visual: Two-branch frequency tree with counts.
articles.proof: Derive from conditional probability; prior choice remains an assumption.

editionPrerequisites: Fractions; conditional probability is refreshed on the page
metadataProvenance.rationale: The background capsule refreshes conditional probability and the product rule before deriving Bayes by natural frequencies. The actual entry assumptions are fraction and percentage arithmetic.
metadataProvenance.levelRationale: Natural-frequency arithmetic and a refreshed conditioning rule suffice; no prior probability course is assumed.

articles.title: A test for independence, not a feeling
articles.hook: Does replacing a token matter on the second draw?
articles.outcome: Check independence through an equality and expose dependence.
articles.formula: A independent of B iff P(A intersect B)=P(A)P(B)
articles.visual: Two draw tables with and without replacement.
articles.proof: Show equality for replacement and counterexample without replacement.

articles.title: Fair games and expected score
articles.hook: Invent a carnival game using paper tokens.
articles.outcome: Compute long-run mean score from outcomes.
articles.visual: Payoff bars with area contributions.
articles.proof: Derive linearity for finite sums; expected value is not promised in one play.

metadataProvenance.rationale: The main route defines random variables, probability-weighted averages and summation notation. Fractions and elementary outcome probabilities are assumed; weighted averages are taught. The optional stopping investigation supplies its own additional background.
metadataProvenance.levelRationale: Finite random variables, linearity of expectation and dependent-score reasoning are Year 1 probability; the optional stopping investigation is explicitly additional.

articles.title: Same average, different surprises
articles.hook: Compare a steady puzzle score with a volatile one.
articles.outcome: Calculate variance and standard deviation for discrete outcomes.
articles.visual: Two distributions with equal mean and different spread.
articles.proof: Expand square to prove identity.

articles.title: How many successes in ten tries?
articles.hook: Ten independent coin flips create a count, not a sequence.
articles.outcome: Use binomial probabilities and identify its assumptions.
articles.visual: Sequence tree collapsing into count bars.
articles.proof: Count sequences with k successes; independence and constant p are explicit.

articles.title: When a bell curve is a useful sketch
articles.hook: A long run of dice sums looks smooth.
articles.outcome: Compare a standardized count with a normal approximation and its limits.
articles.visual: Exact binomial bars overlaid with normal density for several n,p.
articles.proof: State CLT conditions and approximation status; no exact equality is claimed.

metadataProvenance.levelRationale: Standardizes binomial counts and applies a stated CLT with continuity correction; the proof of the CLT is explicitly outside the article.

articles.title: Who is missing from the sample?
articles.hook: A club polls only people who attend a meeting.
articles.outcome: Separate target population, sampling frame and observed sample.
articles.visual: Nested population and frame diagram.
articles.proof: Show an explicit selection-bias counterexample; no general bias correction is claimed.

articles.title: One dataset, several histograms
articles.hook: Rebin a set of puzzle completion times.
articles.outcome: Explain how bin width changes a histogram without changing observations.
articles.visual: Linked dotplot and three bin widths.
articles.proof: Direct tally identity; smooth shape is an exploratory reading.

articles.title: The typical value depends on the question
articles.hook: One exceptionally long song changes the playlist average.
articles.outcome: Contrast mean and median under an outlier.
articles.visual: Movable outlier with two markers.
articles.proof: Calculate both statistics and exhibit outlier sensitivity.

articles.title: Why two honest polls disagree
articles.hook: Sample colored tiles repeatedly from a jar.
articles.outcome: Distinguish parameter, statistic and sampling distribution.
articles.visual: Repeated sample proportions as dots and histogram.
articles.proof: Derive variance under iid assumption; simulation illustrates finite runs.

articles.title: What a 95% confidence interval covers
articles.hook: Many jars have the same hidden color proportion.
articles.outcome: Interpret coverage as a property of the interval procedure.
articles.formula: P_theta(theta in C(X)) approximately 0.95 under stated method
articles.visual: Repeated intervals against fixed hidden parameter.
articles.proof: Derive specified interval under assumptions; avoid posterior claim for realized interval.

articles.title: A p-value is a conditional probability
articles.hook: A supposedly fair spinner lands blue unusually often.
articles.outcome: Compute a tail probability under a named null model.
articles.visual: Null distribution with observed statistic and tail shaded.
articles.proof: Exact finite binomial tail for toy spinner; p is not P(null true).

articles.title: The winner from twenty guesses
articles.hook: Try twenty patterns in random coin tosses and report the most striking.
articles.outcome: Explain how selection inflates false discoveries.
articles.formula: P(at least one p<=alpha)=1-(1-alpha)^m for independent Uniform(0,1) null p-values
articles.visual: Twenty null-test tiles and minimum-p distribution, with exact uniform and discrete-binomial cases distinguished.
articles.proof: Prove exact formula under independent continuous uniform true-null p-values; for independent valid super-uniform p-values it is an upper bound, and dependent tests need separate analysis.

articles.title: Same trend, different story
articles.hook: Track umbrella drawings and rainy days on a shared calendar.
articles.outcome: Interpret correlation as association, inspect shape and confounding.
articles.visual: Four datasets with matched r but different scatterplots.
articles.proof: Compute r; association alone cannot establish cause.

articles.title: When every subgroup wins but the total loses
articles.hook: Compare two fictional puzzle routes across easy and hard boards; the aggregate ranking reverses the within-board ranking.
articles.outcome: Calculate within-group and pooled rates, then explain how unequal group weights reverse the comparison.
articles.formula: pooled rate=sum_g w_g r_g, with group weights w_g summing to 1
articles.visual: Two rate tables linked to weighted bars; a slider changes group allocation while preserving within-group rates.
articles.proof: Exhibit an explicit arithmetic reversal and show the weighted-average mechanism; no causal conclusion follows from aggregation or stratification alone.

editionPrerequisites: Fractions, proportions and weighted averages; all are refreshed on the page
metadataProvenance.rationale: The capsule teaches weighted averages and the worked table teaches two-way denominators. Fraction arithmetic and ordinary averages are assumed; the required transfer tasks solve linear inequalities. The optional potential-outcome investigation introduces its own notation.

articles.title: The line misses in patterned ways
articles.hook: Fit a line to the tempo and length of invented tracks.
articles.outcome: Use residual plots to test a linear description.
articles.visual: Scatterplot linked to residual plot and fitted line.
articles.proof: Least-squares normal-equation sketch; causal and extrapolation claims deferred.

metadataProvenance.levelRationale: Finite least-squares algebra and diagnostic residual calculations; advanced distributional inference is stated only as a boundary.

articles.title: A random walk on a tiny map
articles.hook: A wandering token moves left or right at each chime.
articles.outcome: Enumerate path probabilities and position after steps.
articles.visual: Path tree and endpoint distribution.
articles.proof: Finite enumeration is exact; paths are illustrative samples.

articles.title: How long until the token reaches an edge?
articles.hook: A game piece bounces between two absorbing board edges.
articles.outcome: Set up and solve a small hitting-probability recurrence.
articles.visual: State strip and highlighted absorbing edges.
articles.proof: Solve finite fair-walk case; simulation only checks it.

articles.title: Memory lives in the state
articles.hook: Weather icons on a fictional planet change daily.
articles.outcome: Test whether a proposed state captures the needed history.
articles.visual: History cards and next-state probabilities.
articles.proof: Definition plus counterexample with hidden two-day cycle.

articles.title: A playlist that chooses its next mood
articles.hook: A generative playlist moves among calm, bright and tense moods.
articles.outcome: Advance a distribution with a transition matrix.
articles.visual: Three-node weighted graph and stacked probability bars.
articles.proof: Derive law of total probability for one step.

articles.title: What a Markov chain settles into
articles.hook: Run the mood playlist for a long time.
articles.outcome: Solve stationary probabilities and distinguish them from guaranteed convergence.
articles.visual: Iteration bars beside stationary solution.
articles.proof: Solve finite example; convergence needs irreducibility and aperiodicity.

articles.title: Random arrivals at an imaginary museum
articles.hook: Visitors arrive at a tiny model museum at random times.
articles.outcome: Use a Poisson count model and check rate assumptions.
articles.visual: Event timeline and count histogram.
articles.proof: Derive from stated Poisson-process axioms or small-interval limit; model is illustrative.

articles.title: The next chime has no appointment
articles.hook: Wait for the next event in the toy arrival model.
articles.outcome: Connect exponential waiting times to a Poisson process.
articles.visual: Survival curve and sampled waiting times.
articles.proof: Use zero-count probability to derive survival; lack-of-memory depends on model.

articles.title: Why a short queue sometimes grows
articles.hook: One artist signs imaginary postcards as visitors arrive.
articles.outcome: Model a single-server queue and compare arrival and service rates.
articles.visual: Queue length timeline under two load settings.
articles.proof: State M/M/1 assumptions and stationary result; finite animation is no proof of stability.

articles.title: A family tree that may end
articles.hook: Each fantasy creature leaves 0, 1 or 2 story descendants.
articles.outcome: Calculate expected generation size and extinction in a toy branching process.
articles.visual: Branching trees and extinction-fraction readout.
articles.proof: Derive expectation recursively and fixed-point equation; simulated trees are examples.

articles.title: How surprising is a symbol?
articles.hook: Compare a rare glyph and a common glyph in a made-up alphabet.
articles.outcome: Measure idealized self-information in bits.
articles.visual: Probability slider with bit-height bars.
articles.proof: Derive additivity under independent symbols; probabilities are assumed.

articles.title: Average surprise in a mystery bag
articles.hook: A bag contains symbols with unequal frequencies.
articles.outcome: Compute Shannon entropy and locate the maximum for a binary alphabet.
articles.visual: Entropy curve for a binary source.
articles.proof: Derive the binary maximum at p=1/2 by calculus or concavity; general finite-alphabet maximum is deferred.

articles.title: Two clues can repeat information
articles.hook: Two colored clue cards are drawn together.
articles.outcome: Compare joint and separate uncertainty.
articles.visual: Joint probability heatmap.
articles.proof: Derive chain rule by expanding log joint probability.

articles.title: How much does one clue reveal?
articles.hook: A noisy hint predicts a hidden card suit.
articles.outcome: Compute mutual information and distinguish it from correlation.
articles.visual: Linked contingency table and uncertainty bars.
articles.proof: Prove nonnegativity via KL divergence sketch; estimation bias deferred.

articles.title: Make a code no symbol can confuse
articles.hook: Encode a small fictional alphabet for a secret note.
articles.outcome: Build a prefix-free code and compute its average length.
articles.visual: Binary code tree and encoded string.
articles.proof: Explain unique decoding for prefix codes; optimality of Huffman deferred.

articles.title: Why common symbols get short codes
articles.hook: Compress a tiny set of handmade icons.
articles.outcome: Apply Huffman merging and compare code length with entropy.
articles.visual: Merge tree with weighted leaf depths.
articles.proof: Prove greedy exchange idea in finite case; full theorem optional.

articles.title: A message through a fickle switch
articles.hook: A bit flips with chosen probability in a toy channel.
articles.outcome: Compute output error and conditional uncertainty.
articles.visual: Input-output transition diagram.
articles.proof: Exact channel table calculation; practical communication systems are out of scope.

articles.title: The cost of a wrong probability model
articles.hook: One guessed symbol distribution differs from the bag.
articles.outcome: Calculate KL divergence and explain why it is not a distance.
articles.visual: Two probability bars and log-loss contributions.
articles.proof: State Gibbs inequality and sketch via log u<=u-1; asymmetry by counterexample.

articles.title: The tiny sample looks too predictable
articles.hook: Estimate alphabet entropy from only a handful of draws.
articles.outcome: Observe plug-in estimator bias and report uncertainty.
articles.visual: Sampling histogram of entropy estimates.
articles.proof: Finite-sample bias shown by enumeration for small cases; simulation is illustrative.

articles.title: Two players, four outcomes
articles.hook: Two friends choose independent moves in a tabletop puzzle.
articles.outcome: Read a payoff matrix and separate preference from payoff numbers.
articles.visual: Two-by-two cells with both players’ scores.
articles.proof: Definitions and payoff comparisons are exact for the stated toy game.

articles.title: A move that wins every comparison
articles.hook: A tabletop puzzle gives each player two move options.
articles.outcome: Check strict and weak dominance, including when neither action dominates.
articles.formula: s_i weakly dominates t_i iff u_i(s_i,s_-i)>=u_i(t_i,s_-i) for every s_-i, with > for at least one; strict dominance has > for every s_-i
articles.visual: Highlight row-wise payoff comparisons.
articles.proof: Exhaustive finite comparisons; at least one strict improvement distinguishes weak dominance from payoff equivalence.

articles.title: Stable choices are not always nicest
articles.hook: Players pick paths that can block each other.
articles.outcome: Locate pure Nash equilibria using unilateral deviations.
articles.formula: s* Nash iff u_i(s*)>=u_i(s_i,s*_-i) for every player i and action s_i
articles.visual: Best-response arrows over a payoff grid.
articles.proof: Check all deviations in the finite toy game; existence in pure actions not guaranteed.

articles.title: Why randomize a move?
articles.hook: A hide-and-seek game has no stable pure choice.
articles.outcome: Solve a two-by-two mixed equilibrium by indifference.
articles.formula: E[u_i(a, sigma_-i)]=E[u_i(b, sigma_-i)] on mixed support
articles.visual: Payoff lines crossing as mix probability varies.
articles.proof: Derive for finite two-action example; mixing models strategic uncertainty.

metadataProvenance.levelRationale: Solves two finite indifference equations and checks all pure deviations; no general equilibrium existence proof is required.

articles.title: What changes when play repeats?
articles.hook: The same two-player puzzle is played many evenings.
articles.outcome: Compare one-shot and repeated incentives under a stated discount factor.
articles.visual: Round timeline with strategy branches.
articles.proof: Compute payoff comparison in one toy repeated game; no universal cooperation claim.

articles.title: The group can prefer A to B to C to A
articles.hook: A book club ranks three covers.
articles.outcome: Construct a Condorcet cycle from individual rankings.
articles.formula: A>B, B>C, C>A by pairwise majorities
articles.visual: Three ballots and directed majority cycle.
articles.proof: Enumerate pairwise votes; no theorem about all profiles.

articles.title: Scoring ranked choices changes the winner
articles.hook: Vote on three possible mural colors.
articles.outcome: Compare plurality and Borda counts on the same ballots.
articles.visual: Ballot table and score bars.
articles.proof: Exact tally; fairness depends on chosen criteria.

metadataProvenance.levelRationale: Ranked-ballot scoring and comparison use finite sums and ordering.

articles.title: What Arrow’s theorem actually assumes
articles.hook: Design rules for a fictional club constitution.
articles.outcome: State the domain and conditions behind Arrow’s impossibility theorem.
articles.formula: unrestricted domain + Pareto + IIA + non-dictatorship cannot all hold for >=3 options
articles.visual: Condition cards and counterexample profiles.
articles.proof: State theorem accurately; full proof deferred to course.

metadataProvenance.levelRationale: Illustrates ranking axioms by finite ballots and states Arrow with an explicit proof boundary; the general impossibility proof is not required.

articles.title: Sincere ballots can be unstable
articles.hook: A voter changes a ranking to help a favorite cover.
articles.outcome: Show a manipulable profile for a named rule.
articles.formula: outcome(report_i, reports_-i) compared with outcome(truth_i, reports_-i)
articles.visual: Editable ballot with before-and-after tally.
articles.proof: Give explicit counterexample; no claim that every profile is manipulable.

metadataProvenance.levelRationale: A finite counterexample and a quantified deviation check establish manipulability; broader impossibility results are outside the proof.

articles.title: A model begins with a question
articles.hook: Estimate how many paper tiles cover an imagined wall mural.
articles.outcome: Choose variables, assumptions, units and a checkable output.
articles.formula: tile count approximately area/area per tile
articles.visual: Question-assumption-prediction diagram.
articles.proof: Dimensional check is exact; approximation relies on tile and gap assumptions.

articles.title: Build a miniature gallery that scales
articles.hook: Scale a room drawing while estimating paint area.
articles.outcome: Separate length, area and volume scaling.
articles.visual: Scale slider with linked lengths, areas and volumes.
articles.proof: Derive from products of dimensions for similar shapes.

articles.title: Which assumption matters most?
articles.hook: A toy mural budget depends on tile size and waste.
articles.outcome: Vary one input at a time and compare output change.
articles.visual: Parameter sliders and tornado-style output bars.
articles.proof: Exact for stated formula; local derivative does not cover large nonlinear shifts.

articles.title: Two tones make a slow pulse
articles.hook: Two nearby notes produce a rhythmic beat.
articles.outcome: Use superposition to predict beat frequency.
articles.formula: sin(2pi f1 t)+sin(2pi f2 t)=2 sin(pi(f1+f2)t)cos(pi(f1-f2)t)
articles.visual: Waveform and envelope linked to optional audio.
articles.proof: Trigonometric identity exact; acoustic perception is simplified.

metadataProvenance.levelRationale: Uses the sine sum identity and elementary trigonometric periods, with no calculus requirement.

articles.title: Rules, randomness and repeatability in art
articles.hook: Generate a field of dots with a chosen seed.
articles.outcome: Distinguish deterministic rules, random draws and aesthetic interpretation.
articles.visual: Seeded dot field with density readout.
articles.proof: Uniform sampling statement is model definition; aesthetic judgement is subjective.

articles.title: A rumor on a small fictional network
articles.hook: Colored markers move across a drawn friendship graph.
articles.outcome: Compare network structure under an explicit transmission rule.
articles.formula: P(no transmission to v in step)=product_{u active neighbor}(1-p_uv)
articles.visual: Editable graph and stepwise state table.
articles.proof: Conditional product requires independent edge attempts; simulation is illustrative, not social prediction.

articles.title: A swinging sketch and a linear model
articles.hook: A drawn pendulum decorates a digital clock.
articles.outcome: Compare small-angle linear oscillator with nonlinear pendulum.
articles.formula: theta''+(g/L)sin(theta)=0; for small |theta|, sin(theta) approximately theta
articles.visual: Side-by-side paths with amplitude slider.
articles.proof: Derive small-angle approximation and show mismatch at large angles.

articles.title: A curve can fit and still mislead
articles.hook: Fit several curves to invented gallery visitor counts.
articles.outcome: Distinguish interpolation, extrapolation and mechanism.
articles.visual: Data and competing fitted curves with held-out points.
articles.proof: Residual calculation exact; predictive claim depends on validation design.

metadataProvenance.levelRationale: Compares a line and polynomial by direct substitution and subtraction; no statistical inference is needed.

articles.title: Stress-test a model before sharing it
articles.hook: Predict supplies for a fantasy festival from sparse pilot data.
articles.outcome: Run unit, boundary, sensitivity and held-out checks, then write a limitation note.
articles.visual: Checklist linked to prediction and error table.
articles.proof: Error metrics exact on sample; model validity beyond it remains uncertain.

metadataProvenance.levelRationale: Defines residuals, absolute errors, held-out comparisons and sensitivity using arithmetic and a linear formula.

articles.title: Return to the model: three chances and a remembered draw
articles.hook: What can three pair checks leave undecided, and what does putting a token back actually guarantee?
articles.outcome: Audit pairwise versus mutual independence and a replacement mechanism using exact finite laws, then solve fresh return tasks.
articles.formula: For three events, mutual independence requires all three pair products and the triple product.
articles.visual: Complete eight-ticket and sixteen-ticket word tables, with exact two-colour procedure tables.
articles.proof: Direct finite calculations establish every pair product and a failed triple product; a conditional branch calculation distinguishes replacement from fresh uniform selection.

courses.title: Probability sampler
prerequisites: fractions and simple algebra (local refresher provided)
outcomes: Count finite outcomes and calculate a conditional chance
Explain expected score in a small game
courses.capstone: Design a two-dice card game; count an event, condition on a clue, and calculate expected score.
courses.assessment: Rubric: correct event count, explicit conditioning denominator, correct expected score, and one assumption. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Probability accelerated route
outcomes: Derive Bayes odds from a frequency tree
Check independence and compute moments of a binomial count
courses.capstone: Compare two marble-bag priors and a ten-draw game; show posterior odds, expectation, variance and binomial count.
courses.assessment: Rubric: frequency-tree counts reconcile, prior and posterior are distinguished, binomial assumptions are stated, and variance is computed. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Finite probability and distribution arguments
outcomes: Prove finite probability identities and conditional updates
State the assumptions behind a normal approximation and identify a counterexample
courses.capstone: Write a finite-game probability note proving Bayes odds and moment identities, then compare exact binomial bars with a qualified normal approximation.
courses.assessment: Rubric: finite derivations are valid, approximation conditions are named, a failure case is shown, and simulation is labelled illustrative. Covers all listed articles in this bounded route.

courses.title: Statistics and inference sampler
prerequisites: fractions, graphs and basic probability (local refresher provided)
outcomes: Describe a sample frame and two resistant summaries
Explain why repeated samples give different estimates
courses.capstone: Create a fictional club poll with a biased sampling frame and two honest samples; report summaries and sampling variation.
courses.assessment: Rubric: target and frame are distinct, summaries match displayed data, and sample-to-sample variation is explained. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Statistics and inference accelerated route
outcomes: Interpret interval coverage and a null-model p-value correctly
Inspect correlation, subgroup rates and residuals before describing a trend
courses.capstone: Analyse fictional puzzle-route counts: construct a confidence interval, prespecify a null-tail calculation and show a Simpson reversal.
courses.assessment: Rubric: interval is described by coverage, p-value by its null tail, group rates reconcile with totals, and no causal claim is made. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Sampling, inference and interpretation limits
outcomes: Derive a sampling-variation result and audit multiple testing
Build and critique an inference using assumptions, effect size and uncertainty
courses.capstone: Audit one invented study from frame to residuals: derive a standard error, calculate coverage and p-value under stated models, and construct a confounding counterexample.
courses.assessment: Rubric: assumptions precede calculations, uncertainty and effect size are both reported, a Simpson counterexample is arithmetically sound, and residual limits are clear. Covers all listed articles in this bounded route.

courses.title: Stochastic processes sampler
prerequisites: conditional probability and expected value (local refresher provided)
outcomes: Trace a random walk and explain the Markov state
Translate an arrival story into a count model
courses.capstone: Describe a three-state playlist and a toy arrival timeline; calculate one transition and one Poisson count.
courses.assessment: Rubric: state is sufficient for the proposed next-step rule, transition rows normalize, and arrival-rate units are correct. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Stochastic processes accelerated route
outcomes: Solve a finite hitting probability and iterate a transition matrix
Connect Poisson counts with waiting times under model assumptions
courses.capstone: Build a finite random walk and playlist chain; solve a hitting probability, iterate the matrix and compare an arrival/waiting calculation.
courses.assessment: Rubric: recurrence boundaries are right, matrix multiplication is checked, and Poisson/exponential assumptions are stated. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Finite chains, arrivals and branching models
prerequisites: matrix multiplication and linear equations (bridges provided)
outcomes: Derive and qualify a stationary distribution and queue model
Compare finite simulated paths with recurrence or limit claims
courses.capstone: Analyse a small absorbing walk, a three-state chain and a toy queue; derive recurrence or stationary claims and test one branching extinction equation.
courses.assessment: Rubric: derivations identify conditions for convergence or stability, extinction root is chosen correctly, and finite runs are not used as proof. Covers all listed articles in this bounded route.

courses.title: Information theory sampler
prerequisites: probability, expected value and logarithms (local refresher provided)
outcomes: Calculate surprise and entropy for a small alphabet
Build a uniquely decodable prefix code
courses.capstone: Invent a four-symbol alphabet; calculate surprise and entropy, then draw a valid prefix code.
courses.assessment: Rubric: probabilities sum to one, bit calculations are correct, code is prefix-free, and expected length uses source weights. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Information theory accelerated route
outcomes: Use chain rule and mutual information for noisy clues
Compare Huffman length with entropy for a stipulated distribution
courses.capstone: Send a toy alphabet through a noisy bit switch; compute conditional information and compare two code trees.
courses.assessment: Rubric: joint table normalizes, conditional entropy is computed, code lengths are compared fairly, and noise assumptions are explicit. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Discrete entropy and source coding
outcomes: Prove coding bounds in the finite setting
Distinguish model divergence from metric distance and audit entropy estimates
courses.capstone: Construct a four-symbol source and channel; derive entropy chain rule, a code-length bound and a divergence example, then audit a tiny-sample entropy estimate.
courses.assessment: Rubric: identities have valid algebra, coding bound has its hypotheses, KL asymmetry uses a counterexample, and estimator bias is not ignored. Covers all listed articles in this bounded route.

courses.title: Game theory and social choice sampler
prerequisites: tables, fractions and ordered rankings (local refresher provided)
outcomes: Read a payoff matrix and test unilateral deviations
Construct a three-option majority cycle
courses.capstone: Create a two-by-two puzzle payoff table and a three-cover ballot profile; find best responses and a majority cycle.
courses.assessment: Rubric: payoff comparisons use unilateral changes, pairwise ballot totals are correct, and the cycle is displayed explicitly. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Game theory and social choice accelerated route
outcomes: Solve a two-action mixed equilibrium
Compare voting counts and show a manipulable ballot profile
courses.capstone: Design a hide-and-seek payoff game and a mural-color election; solve a mixed equilibrium and show a strategic ballot.
courses.assessment: Rubric: mixed probabilities make supported actions indifferent, ballot outcome changes are calculated, and incentive claims stay within the toy rules. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Small games and ranked-ballot impossibility
outcomes: State the conditions of Arrow’s theorem precisely
Distinguish equilibrium, welfare and rule design through worked counterexamples
courses.capstone: Write a fictional club constitution comparing three ballot rules and one repeated game; prove small examples and state Arrow’s exact axioms.
courses.assessment: Rubric: equilibrium check is complete, voting rules use the same ballots, Arrow assumptions are stated without overreach, and repeated-game discounting is correct. Covers all listed articles in this bounded route.

courses.title: Mathematical modelling sampler
prerequisites: functions, units and basic probability (local refresher provided)
outcomes: Write assumptions, units and a sensitivity check for a toy model
Use a seeded random-art rule and explain its uncertainty
courses.capstone: Estimate paper tiles for a mural, vary two assumptions and generate a seeded dot composition with a short model note.
courses.assessment: Rubric: units are consistent, assumptions are visible, sensitivity changes use the stated formula, and seeded output is reproducible. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Mathematical modelling accelerated route
outcomes: Derive a beat envelope and model a network spread rule
Compare fit with held-out performance and a limitation note
courses.capstone: Model a two-tone beat and a toy network spread; compare formulas, simulation and held-out checks under changed parameters.
courses.assessment: Rubric: beat formula is correct, network edge independence is stated, simulation labels are clear, and validation uses held-out data. Covers selected articles only.

courses.title: Toy models from assumption to validation
outcomes: Derive one approximation and test its boundary
Validate and communicate a model through residual, sensitivity and assumption checks
courses.capstone: Build a miniature sound-and-network exhibit: derive a beat or small-angle equation, test sensitivity and residuals, then write a validation and limits memo.
courses.assessment: Rubric: approximation range is named, model equations and units agree, sensitivity and residual checks are reproducible, and limits are candid. Covers all listed articles in this bounded route.

labs.title: Reveal the denominator
labs.readout: Frequency tree, exact posterior and simulated estimate
labs.invariant: Posterior probabilities sum to 1; empirical frequencies approach values only with enough independent draws
labs.pitfalls: A likelihood is not a posterior; zero-probability evidence cannot be conditioned on
labs.accessibleFallback: Full branch-count table, formulas, keyboard controls and static worked cases

labs.title: Build a fair or lopsided game
labs.readout: Exact expectation and variance beside simulated running averages
labs.invariant: Probabilities sum to 1; exact mean is unchanged by trial count
labs.pitfalls: A small simulation can wander far from expectation
labs.accessibleFallback: Data table, exact arithmetic and downloadable text transcript

labs.title: Watch interval coverage
labs.readout: Intervals that cover fixed parameter, observed coverage and nominal target
labs.invariant: Coverage claim concerns the method under its sampling assumptions
labs.pitfalls: A realized interval is not assigned a 95% posterior probability
labs.accessibleFallback: Text list of intervals with cover/miss flags and summary counts

labs.title: Explore null tails and selection
labs.readout: Exact binomial tail and simulated minimum p-value distribution
labs.pitfalls: p-value is not P(null true); choosing direction afterward changes the test; the exact familywise formula requires independent uniform null p-values.
labs.accessibleFallback: Exact probability table, keyboard tail selection and text histogram

labs.title: Walk until an edge
labs.readout: Exact finite hitting probability and sampled paths
labs.invariant: Absorbing states remain absorbing; probabilities total 1
labs.pitfalls: Finite runs cannot establish eventual absorption or exact probability
labs.accessibleFallback: Path table, recurrence solution and pauseable step controls

labs.title: Playlist mood chain
labs.readout: Distribution by step and stationary candidate
labs.invariant: Every transition row sums to 1; distribution stays normalized
labs.pitfalls: Stationarity does not ensure convergence when chain is periodic or reducible
labs.accessibleFallback: Transition table, iteration table and plain-language state descriptions

labs.title: Mix an alphabet
labs.readout: Surprise bars, entropy and conditional entropy
labs.pitfalls: Observed sample frequencies differ from stipulated probabilities
labs.accessibleFallback: Editable probability table and computed values with formulas

labs.title: Code a tiny alphabet
labs.readout: Prefix tree, code lengths, expected length and entropy
labs.invariant: No leaf code is prefix of another; Kraft sum <= 1
labs.pitfalls: Entropy is a lower bound on ideal average length, not an achieved length for every finite code
labs.accessibleFallback: Tree as indented text and full encode/decode transcript

labs.title: Follow the best-response arrows
labs.readout: Pure equilibrium cells and expected payoff lines
labs.invariant: Marked pure equilibria pass every unilateral deviation check
labs.pitfalls: An equilibrium need not maximize joint payoff
labs.accessibleFallback: Payoff table with best-response labels and keyboard-selectable cells

labs.title: Count the same ballots three ways
labs.readout: Plurality, Borda and pairwise outcomes with cycle indicator
labs.invariant: Every ballot ranks each option once; totals reconcile with voter count
labs.pitfalls: Arrow theorem applies to stated ranking and fairness axioms, not a claim all voting is pointless
labs.accessibleFallback: Ballot table, pairwise count table and textual winner explanations

labs.title: Two tones and a beat envelope
labs.readout: Wave sum, envelope period and exact frequency difference
labs.invariant: For equal-amplitude sinusoidal tones, algebraic superposition identity holds
labs.pitfalls: The simple model ignores timbre and hearing context
labs.accessibleFallback: Numeric sample table, waveform description, optional muted audio and no autoplay

labs.title: Stress-test a toy network model
labs.readout: Outcome spread, sensitivity summary and model assumption card
labs.invariant: Node count bounded by graph size; fixed seed reproduces a run
labs.pitfalls: Simulation explores chosen rule, not real-world social behavior or causal impact
labs.accessibleFallback: Adjacency list, per-step state table and numeric sensitivity results
